question.problem:
Find the binormal vector to the curve $r(t)$ at an arbitrary point, given that

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{1}{3}⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡(t+1),2\sqrt{2},\operatorname{cos}⁡(t+1)⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $T$ denotes the unit tangent vector.
question.worked_solution:
The binormal vector is given by

$$
B(t)=T(t)\times N(t),
$$

where the principal normal vector $N(t)$ is given by

$$
N(t)=\frac{{T}^{′}(t)}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find the principal normal $N(t).$ To do this, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and its magnitude as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{1}{3}⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(t+1)),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\sqrt{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(t+1))⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{3}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(t+1),\,0,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡(t+1)⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\frac{1}{3}\sqrt{(\operatorname{cos}⁡(t+1))^{2}+{(0)}^{2}+{(-\operatorname{sin}⁡(t+1))}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\sqrt{{cos}^{2}⁡(t+1)+{sin}^{2}⁡(t+1)} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we normalize ${T}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}N(t) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(t)}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{\frac{1}{3}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(t+1),\,0,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡(t+1)⟩}{(\frac{1}{3})}=⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(t+1),\,0,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡(t+1)⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the binormal vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}B(t) & =T(t)\times N(t) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡(t+1),2\sqrt{2},\operatorname{cos}⁡(t+1)⟩\times ⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(t+1),\,0,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡(t+1)⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\,\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(t+1) & 2\sqrt{2} & \operatorname{cos}⁡(t+1) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(t+1) & 0 & -\operatorname{sin}⁡(t+1)\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}2\sqrt{2} & \operatorname{cos}⁡(t+1) \\ 0 & -\operatorname{sin}⁡(t+1)\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(t+1) & \operatorname{cos}⁡(t+1) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(t+1) & -\operatorname{sin}⁡(t+1)\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(t+1) & 2\sqrt{2} \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(t+1) & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,k\text{ }] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}⟨-2\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(t+1)-0,-(-{sin}^{2}⁡(t+1)-{cos}^{2}⁡(t+1)),0-2\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(t+1)⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{3}⟨-2\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(t+1),\,1,\,-2\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(t+1)⟩\end{aligned}
$$
